pairs.why: Nearly identical rockets, but A has a slightly softer, painted finish and gentler highlights, while B's nose cone and body look more glossy and plastic, the statue-like look the lessons marked down.
Same build in both; A's shading is a little softer and less specular, which is closer to the real cards' smooth painted surfaces than B's shinier, toy-plastic sheen.
The shapes match, but B's harder gloss and more saturated cyan sky look less like the real cards than A's softer light and more natural sky.
A's slightly matte, painterly white body and softer clouds read closer to the real airplane and balloons; B leans glossier and more plastic.
The two are almost the same; A has slightly gentler highlights on the nose and fins, and B's stronger gloss pushes it toward the overly shiny look.
Construction and color are identical; A's softer specular finish fits the real cards a little better than B's glossier rendering.
A has softer light on the body and fins, in line with the real cards; B's brighter specular hits make it look slightly more plastic.
There is very little difference, but A's finish is a touch less glossy and its sky is more natural, which is closer to the real cards than B.
